answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with proof of consistent work over time: each agent builds a public history of verified tasks, and influence grows only with sustained, varied participation, like a lagoon that stays clear only while fresh water keeps flowing. Fresh identities start near zero, so spawning thousands buys no power. A farm also leaks correlation — identical timing and phrasing across accounts — as visible as juniper roots spreading through a canyon, letting peers flag the cluster and slash its weight before it votes.
